passive.label: Passive Flexion + overpressure with FADIR (adduction + IR at end-flexion)

findings: Resisted tests usually normal — not a contractile pattern
Passive FADIR (flexion + adduction + IR at end-flexion) with overpressure reproduces groin pain/click
sttt.interpretation: The passive FADIR provocation, not resisted testing, is what reproduces symptoms here — consistent with a labral/impingement source rather than a contractile lesion.

cpa.pattern: A Hip Extension Firing Order pattern for a QL/hamstring-dominant compensation. Fascial component (from source): Anterior hip capsule / adductor fascia.

kineticChain.name: Hip Internal Rotation Mobility
kineticChain.chainEffect: Moderately restricted (20–29°) internal rotation is explicitly documented as consistent with FAI, where the FADIR test is likely positive.

functionalScreen.name: Seated Hip Rotation (FAI + capsular screen)
functionalScreen.note: The named functional test for exactly this pattern. FMA source note: FADIR & deep squat reproduce groin pain/click.

H02.name: Hip Osteoarthritis
keyExams: Passive hip ROM with end-feel (capsular pattern)

findings: Passive IR most restricted — capsular pattern IR = Flexion = Abduction
sttt.interpretation: A capsular pattern (IR = Flexion = Abduction) with a hard/bony end-feel and painless resisted testing is consistent with osteoarthritic capsular restriction rather than a contractile lesion.

cpa.pattern: Check the Hip Extension Firing Order (often QL- or hamstring-dominant). Fascial component (from source): Global hip capsular fascial restriction.

kineticChain.name: Hip Internal Rotation Mobility
kineticChain.chainEffect: Severely restricted, often <20° with significant asymmetry — matching the capsular-pattern IR loss on passive testing above.

functionalScreen.name: Seated Hip Rotation

fields.label: Seated Hip Rotation
options: Bilateral, more severe restriction, hard/bony end-feel (OA)

functionalScreen.note: Same test as FAI, but expect bilateral, more severe restriction with a hard/bony end-feel. FMA source note: Capsular-pattern loss (IR/flexion); squat & stairs limited.

findings: Resisted abduction strong but painful at the trochanter
Passive adduction (Ober-type stretch) reproduces lateral pain
sttt.interpretation: Strong-but-painful resisted abduction localizing to the trochanter, plus a positive Ober-type passive stretch, is the classic contractile (tendon) pattern for gluteal tendinopathy.

cpa.pattern: The textbook GTPS driver — confirm via therapy localization (touch TFL, retest glute med). Fascial component (from source): Lateral line (ITB/TFL) tension.

kineticChain.name: Hip Abduction Mobility & Stability (Trendelenburg + Ober's)
kineticChain.chainEffect: Documents both the mobility restriction and the stability deficit — the direct match for lateral hip pathology.

functionalScreen.name: Single Leg Squat + Lateral Step Down

fields.label: Single Leg Squat (glute med / dynamic valgus)

functionalScreen.note: Both are the app's named functional tests for this exact pattern. FMA source note: Single-leg stance 30s & resisted abduction reproduce lateral pain.

resisted.label: Resisted Hip Extension (knee extended, adding hamstring)

findings: Resisted hip extension (knee extended) strong but painful at the ischium — classic contractile pattern
Passive hip flexion with knee extended also reproduces pain
sttt.interpretation: Strong-but-painful resisted extension localizing to the ischium is the classic Cyriax contractile-lesion pattern for the proximal hamstring origin.

cpa.pattern: The classic driver: hamstrings become the primary hip extensor and get overloaded. Fascial component (from source): Posterior-chain (hamstring–sacrotuberous) fascia.

kineticChain.name: Hip Extension Mobility (Thomas Test)
kineticChain.chainEffect: Provides posterior-chain context, but the Prone Hip Extension functional test below is the more direct diagnostic tool for this condition.

functionalScreen.name: Prone Hip Extension (glute max firing pattern, Janda)
functionalScreen.note: Palpate glute max vs hamstring during the test — hamstring firing first/dominating is the direct functional correlate of this condition. FMA source note: Bent-knee stretch / long-lever resisted knee-flexion reproduce pain.

H05.name: Adductor-Related Groin Pain (Adductor Strain / Athletic Pubalgia)

findings: Resisted adduction strong but painful at the pubic origin — the squeeze test is this same resisted test
Passive abduction (stretch) also reproduces groin pain
sttt.interpretation: Strong-but-painful resisted adduction localizing to the pubic origin, reproduced by the squeeze test, is the classic contractile pattern for adductor-related groin pain.

cpa.pattern: Typically compensating for an inhibited Glute Max — check the Hip Extension Firing Order. Fascial component (from source): Adductor / deep-front-line fascia.

kineticChain.reason: No hip KC test isolates pure adduction in this app's library (IR/ER/extension/abduction are covered, not adduction specifically) — rely on the resisted/CPA findings above.

functionalScreen.name: Hip Hinge Pattern or Single Leg Squat

fields.label: Single Leg Squat (compensatory pattern under loaded groin activity)

functionalScreen.note: Either test screens for compensatory patterns during loaded groin activity; choose per presentation. FMA source note: Resisted adduction (squeeze test) & change-of-direction reproduce pain.

passive.label: FAIR Test (passive hip flexion + adduction + IR)

findings: Resisted ER (piriformis) reproduces deep buttock pain
FAIR test (passive flexion + adduction + IR) is positive — the key provocation
sttt.interpretation: Resisted ER reproducing deep buttock pain, combined with a positive FAIR test, localizes the lesion to the piriformis/deep gluteal space.

muscles.name: Piriformis
muscles.state: Overactive, glute med compensation (or glute max)

cpa.pattern: Always check Glute Med/Glute Max facilitation before treating piriformis alone. Fascial component (from source): Deep gluteal fascial compartment; sciatic neural bias.

kineticChain.name: Hip External Rotation Mobility
kineticChain.chainEffect: Restricted external rotation with deep buttock pain is explicitly documented as consistent with piriformis syndrome, where the FAIR test is likely positive.

functionalScreen.name: Seated Hip Rotation (IR/ER range screen)
functionalScreen.note: Cross-reference against the FAIR-test finding above.

H07.name: Snapping Hip Syndrome (Coxa Saltans, Internal or External)
keyExams: Dynamic snapping hip test (observe/palpate active flexion-extension)

findings: Resisted hip flexion (iliopsoas type) or resisted abduction (ITB type) may reproduce the snap
Mostly a dynamic/observational finding rather than a static resisted one
sttt.interpretation: These resisted tests are secondary here — the dynamic snapping hip test (active flexion-extension) is the primary provocation for this condition, per the source.

cpa.pattern: Check Glute Med facilitation in both types. Fascial component (from source): Lateral line (external) or iliopsoas (internal) fascia.

kineticChain.name: Hip Abduction Mobility (external/TFL type) or Hip Extension Mobility / Thomas Test (internal/iliopsoas type)

fields.label: Hip Extension Mobility / Thomas Test (internal/iliopsoas type)

kineticChain.chainEffect: Select per the suspected snapping structure — external (ITB) vs internal (iliopsoas).

functionalScreen.name: Single Leg Squat or Hip Hinge Pattern

fields.label: Dynamic snap observed during loaded movement

functionalScreen.note: Observing the dynamic snap during a loaded functional movement is more revealing than any static positional test for this condition.
